You could lose your savings to one text, before you see why it never looks like a scam.
Here are the three texts that do it. And the one rule that beats all three.
One. Your package couldn't be delivered. Update your address. The link looks like the courier. It isn't.
Two. Did you make this purchase? Reply NO to cancel. Reply, and a bank agent calls you within minutes.
Three. Hi Mum, I lost my phone, this is my new number. The next message asks for money.
The rule. Never tap a link in a text. Close it, and open your bank or courier app yourself. That's the whole defence.
Send this to the person in your family who'd fall for number three.
